atendimentos.pergunta: What is the difference between expiration and storage conditions?

resposta.mensagem:
The expiration date indicates the manufacturer's stated time interval during which the product is expected to maintain its quality and characteristics, provided it is handled and stored correctly. Storage conditions refer to the specific environmental requirements—such as temperature, humidity, protection from direct sunlight, or refrigeration—needed to keep the product properly preserved.

A valid date alone only permits an assessment of the stated time interval and does not guarantee food safety, approval for consumption, or legal certification. Contamination, package damage, or inadequate storage can make an unexpired product unfit for consumption before its expiration date. Conversely, expired products must not be offered for sale or consumed. Always inspect the packaging, verify that recommended storage instructions have been maintained, and contact the shop or manufacturer if you notice any damage or irregularities.
